assumptions: source assumption: operational scope - actual/realistic operating and support environment; includes logistics time, ready time, waiting/administrative downtime plus preventive and corrective maintenance.
MTBF and MDT in consistent time units; steady-state (limiting) availability.
MDT quantities are under logistician/mission-planner control (spares, tools, manpower proximity), unlike designer-controlled inherent terms.

gaps: Meanings operational_availability/mean_downtime absent from runtime vocabulary; scalar form fits engine once meanings exist.
Same algebraic form as the inherent record with different quantities: bind MDT (with logistics) vs MTTR (corrective only) deliberately, never interchangeably.

models.inverse_notes: MTBF = Ao*MDT/(1-Ao) needs Ao != 1; MDT = MTBF*(1-Ao)/Ao needs Ao != 0. Check: Ao=0.99998,MDT=2 gives MTBF = 99998 (estimate scale of 100000). Algebraic only.
limitations: Same equation shape as inherent availability is not the same model: MDT versus MTTR scope differs; misbinding overstates fielded availability.
MDT aggregates heterogeneous delay sources; splitting them needs logistics modeling beyond this record.
MTBF/MDT are estimated inputs with uncertainty; never measured claims about real systems.

references.method: Ordinary case at transducer scale: 100000/100002 = 0.99998. Same arithmetic as the inherent record but MDT-quantity scope; expected keeps computed value.
references.provenance: Independent arithmetic check with source-scale inputs.

references.method: Materially different scale with heavy logistics share: 500/550 = 0.9090909; shows MDT dominating the quotient.
references.provenance: Independent arithmetic check with synthetic inputs.

references.method: Boundary: zero mean downtime collapses operational onto certain availability; admitted ideal boundary (instant support).

rejection_cases.reason: MTBF is required alongside MDT; omitting it leaves Ao undetermined.
